_note: PURGED AND REBUILT 2026-08-23 (Ben): the hot file holds only the items of the earliest incomplete sprint - Sprint 16, the mercenary vertical slice (v0.1.15). Every item that existed before (530, ids <= BL-568) is snapshotted verbatim in archive/backlog-purged-2026-08-23.json and is NOT open work. New items name their sprint in `sprint`. File nothing here that the open sprint does not need; when the sprint closes, the next sprint's items are authored fresh against the authority docs. Ids never reuse.
Canonical backlog for Project Io — the authoritative METADATA index of every backlog item.
One item = one object in `items`.
STATUS (authoritative; JSON wins over any prose/glyph disagreement):
designed    (glyph ✓) — design settled, promote-ready.
design-owed (glyph ~) — design still owed; must be settled before promotion.
PRIORITY (ascending): F C B A S SSS.
F=deferred/parked, C=low, B=medium, A=important, S=high, SSS=do-immediately.
`parked:true` is the explicit flag for F-priority items.
DIFFICULTY (1-5): 1=~5min, 2=~20min, 3=~1h, 4=~3h, 5=~12h+ (break a 5 down).
SEQUENCING: `requires` lists BL-XXX ids of backlog items that must land first (supercedes the
old `waits_on` short_name list — v2 schema 2026-06-17). `blocked_on` names a truly-external
prerequisite with no backlog item (third-party dep, real-world gate). An item can be `designed`
and still have unmet `requires`. Both fields are nullable; [] means no dependencies.
WORKFLOW: a `designed` item is PROMOTED into REFINED.md and DELIVERED (see DELIVERY.md).
A `design-owed` item is DESIGNED first (prose settled in `design` field, status flipped).
When work lands, the item is RETAINED here under the terminal status `complete` with a
resolution/completion_note, and design propagates into the authority doc. (Convention updated
2026-07-04: terminal items were once removed; the tooling — gyre.py, progress counts — now
depends on them staying. Do not delete landed entries.)
(Terminal status normalised 2026-08-01: `complete` is the only one. `shipped` was a
synonym with no defined difference — written only by tools/session/ship_items.js and
apply_session_close.js, which now write `complete`; the six items carrying it were
converted. Readers still tolerate the old value, so nothing breaks on an old branch.)
DESIGN PROSE — the `design` field (policy updated 2026-06-17):
- ALL items: prose lives in the `design` field here, not in BACKLOG.md.
- NEW items: author prose here directly. No BACKLOG.md body.
- LEGACY items (pre-2026-06-17): `design: "@BACKLOG.md"` means prose is still in markdown.
Migrate to this field on first edit (design settle or promotion) — do not wait for promotion.
On migration: write prose here, replace the BACKLOG.md body with a tombstone line.
- ON PROMOTION into REFINED.md: delete any remaining BACKLOG.md body (if not yet migrated).
- BACKLOG.md therefore only drains, never grows, and is deleted once empty.
- For designs with rich tables use markdown in the `design` string (tables render fine).
- `design: "@<doc>"` is also valid as a pointer to an authority doc when prose lives there.
VERSION GOAL (policy added 2026-07-08): every NEW item names which version it is FOR via the
`version_goal` field — the minor it targets ("v0.0.9"), the next one ("v0.1.0"), or
"post-v0.1.0" for anything beyond the prototype's remaining arc (see ROADMAP.md for the
live version sequence and themes). This is a goal, not a promise — it may slip a version at
re-sequencing, same as priority. Legacy items predating this policy are not backfilled; treat
a missing `version_goal` as "unset (legacy)", not as "post-v0.1.0".
ARCHIVE — the hot/cold split (policy added 2026-08-02):
This file is the METADATA INDEX and is read ACROSS items far more often than INTO one.
So when an item lands, its narrative fields — design, resolution, completion_note,
progress_note — MOVE OUT to docs/development/archive/backlog-design-<quarter>.json.
The item keeps `design: "@<that path>"` (the pointer form blessed above) plus an
`archived` field naming the cold file. This is the authority time-slice made physical:
backlog.json owns the item while it is open; the cold store and the subject authority
doc own it once it has landed.
- Run it: tools/session/archive_designs.js (Delivery close step, after ship_items.js).
- Read it back: tools/session/backlog_query.js --full, or backlog_view.js — both resolve
the pointer transparently, so an archived item reads exactly like a hot one.
- Reverse it: archive_designs.js --restore [BL-XXX ...]. Nothing is ever deleted.
- AMEND A LANDED ITEM'S PROSE IN THE COLD FILE, not here — the hot file has no copy.
- backlog_lint.js FAILS on an `archived` pointer with no record behind it, and WARNS
when frozen history climbs back over 30% of this file.
AUTHOR (policy added 2026-08-22): items may carry an `author` field naming who
proposed the item (e.g. "Joe"). Informational only — no effect on status, priority,
or workflow. Nullable; missing/null means unattributed (legacy items). Design
brainstorms that haven't yet become a backlog item live in docs/development/design/.

items.title: The ancient arc reaches five output goods and needs more — append the roster’s new resource values and pay the save bump
items.summary: Measured: the ancient band produces five distinct goods — charcoal, iron_blooms, steel, trade_goods_misc, food_rations — across eight recipes. A wide roster cannot be authored over that set without every new building making something that already exists. RULING 2026-08-23 (Ben): yes, add goods and pay the version bump. This item is the enum append, the price table and the save bump, done ONCE so the roster items that follow stay pure Lua.
items.design:
## Why this is its own item, and why it is first

Appending a `resource_type` value stopped being free on 2026-08-22, when the save format landed: every per-resource array is sized off `resource_count`, so an append changes every array length and is a format break. `components.hpp` says so at the enum.

Doing it once, deliberately, ahead of the roster work keeps the rest of the sprint out of `world_save.cpp` entirely.

**Sequencing is load-bearing.** Sprint 16 bumps `world_save_version` (3 → 4) in three of its own items. This item takes the NEXT number and must not begin until Sprint 16 has merged to main (Ben’s sequencing ruling, 2026-08-23). Starting early means two sprints minting the same version number for different formats.

## Work

1. Append the goods the wide roster needs, at the END of the enum, never inserted. First cut, each earning its place by being consumed by an authored recipe in BL-586 (the admission rule, PRODUCTION.md): `hides`, `leather`, `cloth`, `ceramics`, `tools`, `dressed_stone`, `planks`. Seven values; the exact set is settled WITH BL-586’s chains, not before — a good with no consumer does not get in.
2. `world_gen.lua` `base_price` for each. Price is DERIVED from the input basket at the processing roster’s observed output:input ratio, not picked — `recipes.lua`’s note at the ordnance entry states the method.
3. `world_save_version` bump, and the read path’s strict-equality rejection. No migration of old saves: the header exists precisely to refuse a mismatch (`world_save.hpp`).
4. `chain_depth`’s R1/R1b rows re-run — every new value must be obtainable AND wanted in the same band, or it does not ship.

## The rule this item does not get to bend

BL-286 put eleven goods in the enum with their behaviours “unfiled”; five were deleted twelve days later, having been produced by nothing and consumed by nothing. That deletion is why `resource_type` is clean today. Nothing here lands ahead of its consumer.

items.title: Seven named ancient buildings is not a roster — author the chains that make the 0 CE product wide
items.summary: RULING 2026-08-23 (Ben): a full content sprint. Measured today: eight recipes carry era = "ancient", giving seven named processing buildings — Charcoal Burner, Peat Kiln, Bloomery, Smithy (steel), Smithy (ordnance), Potter & Weaver, Glassworks, Miller. This item authors the chains that take that to a real roster, on the existing three building_type values, following the pattern PRODUCTION.md already records.
items.design:
## The pattern, restated because it is the whole method

A named building is a recipe, or an extraction target, on a generic `building_type` — distinguished by placement rule and glyph, not by an enum value. Mint a new `building_type` only where BL-325’s test is met: a distinct placement rule AND a distinct glyph AND behaviour no recipe can express. The military base passed that test. A tannery does not.

## The chains to author

Each line is a named building; each declares its group (BL-434, sub-facility groups) and its `era = "ancient"` tag. Depths follow from the graph and are never authored:

| Building | Chain | Group |
|---|---|---|
| Tannery | hides → leather | Artisan Goods |
| Weaver | (split out of Potter & Weaver) fibre → cloth | Artisan Goods |
| Potter | clay → ceramics | Artisan Goods |
| Sawmill | timber → planks | Construction Materials (new group) |
| Stonemason | stone → dressed_stone | Construction Materials |
| Toolmaker | iron_blooms + planks → tools | Metal Foundry |
| Shipwright | planks + cloth → a terminal trade good | Advanced Fabrication |

`hides` comes from a pasture / hunting extraction target — the endemic `furs` tier already proves that extraction shape works.

The exact list is content work and will move at authoring. The **admission rule is the invariant**: no building whose output nothing consumes, no good no building consumes. `chain_depth`’s R1/R1b enforces it, and must be green at the end of every slice, not only at the end of the item.

## Depth is the point, not a side effect

Ancient max depth is **3** today, on one chain (timber → charcoal → blooms → steel). A roster that is wide and FLAT is twenty ways to do the same shallow thing — BL-429’s slice-1 note says exactly this, and it is the trap to avoid. Every chain above should reach depth 2 or better; the Toolmaker (blooms + planks) is deliberately the deepest, at 4.

## Glyphs

`icons::building()` keys off the identity resource — an extraction site’s target, a processing facility’s primary output — so each NEW GOOD needs a glyph, not each new building. Two buildings reaching the same good share one by design (ICONS.md § 1c). Budget: one glyph per BL-585 value.

## Owed alongside the code

Placement rules for any target that is not simply “has a deposit”; `k_extractable` updated for every new extraction target — BL-429 slice 2 found `peat` authored on tiles but missing from that array, so no site could ever have targeted it; and PRODUCTION.md § The ancient chain rewritten to the new table.

items.title: There is not one genuine alternate production method in the roster — every sibling pair is a supply route
items.summary: The measurement that overturns NR-243 rather than answering it. chain_depth’s R2 buckets every same-output sibling pair as a supply route (disjoint raws), a named precondition pair, or a genuine interchangeable method — and the third bucket is EMPTY. So the 2026-08-15 ruling ("alternates with real trade-offs") is mechanism without content: the Method page offers siblings, but no two of them are a choice a corp can actually make on one tile. This item authors the missing bucket.
items.design:
## What was measured, and what it corrects

PRODUCTION.md § Alternate production methods still reports four dominated sibling pairs as “Ben’s open call (NR-243)”. **That text is stale.** The guard that found them was retracted on 2026-08-16 and replaced: `recipe_switch_harness.cpp` records the retraction in its own header, and `chain_depth.cpp`’s R2 is the replacement.

All four were false positives of grouping by (primary output, era band). `steel_from_iron_nickel` vs `steel`, `peat_charcoal` vs `charcoal` and `glass` vs `trade_goods` have **disjoint raws** — which one a corp runs is decided by deposit access, not by price. The propellant pair is an explicitly named atmosphere-versus-airless precondition.

The live consequence is the opposite of a balance defect: with every pair bucketed as a route or an exemption, **no pair is a method at all**, and the no-dominance rule has nothing to guard.

## What an interchangeable method actually is

Two recipes on one building, sharing at least one input, either of which a corp on a given tile could genuinely run. Ben, 2026-08-23: *“it’s not always clear that a more advanced method is better (depending on which market it builds to).”* So the axis is which market the output is going to, not which route is stronger:

  * **Ratio** — a Bloomery and a larger furnace both take `iron_ore + charcoal`, differing in fuel-per-unit against throughput. Cheap fuel favours one, cheap ore the other.
  * **Yield split** — a method with a second, lesser output: worth more where that byproduct has a market, worthless where it does not.
  * **Labour against materials** — a hand method cheap to build and dear to run; the powered one inverts it. Note the constraint: `base_wage` lives on `building_economics`, keyed by TYPE, so this axis needs the rate on the recipe or the cost on the named building (BL-590) — there is no wage per method today.

First cut: **three** genuine method pairs, at least one of them ancient, each authored with the market condition under which it wins stated in a comment beside it.

## The guard must grow with the content

R2 compares one fixed reference-price snapshot. A method that is only better “depending on which market it builds to” is invisible to a single snapshot — it will read as dominated. R2 gains a second price vector, and asserts each genuine method wins under at least one. That is the mechanical form of the ruling; the guard work itself is BL-592.

## What this item deliberately does NOT do

It deletes nothing. The 2026-08-23 ruling to “delete the dominated sibling” was taken on the stale doc text above, and the four pairs it names are not dominated. Deleting them would remove the coal Smelter, the Charcoal Burner, the Potter & Weaver and the airless propellant route for no measured reason — and would strand `sand`, `peat` and `iron_nickel_ore` as orphans, failing R1 in the same pass. Recorded as a correction rather than acted on; re-rule if the deletion is still wanted.
items.resolution: Two genuine interchangeable methods authored on the existing resource roster: charcoal_from_kiln (Coking Kiln, ancient) and steel_bessemer (Bessemer Converter, industrial). chain_depth R2: 2 methods, 0 dominated (was 0 methods before). recipe_switch_harness and price_band_harness re-verified clean. PRODUCTION.md corrected — NR-243 closed rather than retuned (NR-589).
items.completion_note: Built standalone ahead of Sprint 16 merging: the only Sprint 17 item with zero file overlap against Sprint 16 (scripts/recipes.lua, tools/verify/chain_depth.cpp, docs/economy/PRODUCTION.md — none in Sprint 16's set). requirements.json group interchangeable-methods-exist, all 3 rows complete.

items.title: A tech can unlock a building type but not a recipe — the effect union needs its third arm
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-23: "include the notion of progression in different methods ... most building types, and most recipes are not buildable on game start." Measured: tech_effect has exactly two arms — unlock a building_type, or move a scalar — so a tech cannot reach a recipe at all. And exactly ONE gate is authored (E0-ML-01, the military base) against ~150 inert nodes in tech_tree.lua, which says of itself that nothing in the simulation reads it. This item adds the arm, and enough authored gates that the roster is earned rather than handed over.
items.design:
## The measurement

`tech_effect_kind` is `unlock_structure` | `modify_scalar` (`tech_gate.hpp`). `prototype_tech_gates()` returns **one** gate. `scripts/tech_tree.lua` opens with *DATA ONLY — the tech system is post-prototype; nothing in the simulation reads this.* So the only earned lock in the economy today is `depth_locked`, and it applies only to recipes tagged `era = "ancient"`.

## Work

1. A third arm, `tech_effect_kind::unlock_recipe`, carrying a recipe **name** — not an id. Recipe ids are positional and stored in `building_component.recipe`; a gate that outlives a roster edit must not silently repoint. Mirror field alongside `unlocks_structure`, authored only through `add_effect`, exactly as the existing arms are.
2. `recipe_unlocked(w, corp, recipe_id)` beside `structure_unlocked`.
3. **Read at both doors**, exactly as the depth gate is: `construct_building` guards placement, `try_switch_recipe` guards retooling. Guarding only placement leaves the one-click bypass the depth gate already documents — place the shallow method, then retool onto the gated sibling in the same group.
4. `construction_result::tech_locked` and `recipe_switch_result` gain the recipe case; `corp_command_result::rejected_tech_locked` is reused, so an agent cannot tell a structure lock from a recipe lock on the seam. The three locks stay distinct in MEANING, and that distinction is already documented: `era_locked` never available, `tech_locked` earned by research, `depth_locked` earned by building.
5. **The Build door and the scorer must filter on it.** `corp_ai.cpp` walks the whole processing roster picking best net margin, filtering on era and depth only; an unfiltered tech-locked recipe would have every rival scoring a candidate the seam then refuses. The door filters for the same reason it filters depth — the door does not offer what the gate would refuse.
6. Author the gates: a first cut across BL-586’s chains, predicates written in `condition_set` against what a corp has already DONE — structures held, goods produced, surplus — never a timer.

## The design constraint Ben set

This is not a reshaping of the tech tree; the ~150 nodes stay as they are. What changes is that some of them resolve. And an unlocked method is **not a strict upgrade** (BL-587): earning it opens a different trade, so the tree expresses progression without expressing power.

items.title: Six of eight building types and every ancient recipe but one are buildable on turn one
items.summary: Ben, 2026-08-23: "most building types, and most recipes are not buildable on game start." Measured against that: of the eight building types only the launchpad (era) and the military base (tech) are withheld, and of the eight ancient recipes only the Bloomery chain sits above required depth 0 — so a fresh ancient corp is offered nearly the whole roster in its first minute. This item makes the opening narrow, and asserts it.
items.design:
## What a fresh ancient corp sees today

The Build door collapses processing to one row per GROUP (BL-434), so an ancient campaign shows four processing rows — Metal Foundry, Food Processing, Fuel Production, Artisan Goods — plus one extraction row per extractable deposit on the tile, plus four infrastructure rows. Of those, only Metal Foundry’s ancient members are depth-gated, and even that group stays visible because its representative can be an `any`-band recipe (`refined_copper`), which the depth filter deliberately never touches.

## Work

1. **A stated opening set.** Name the buildings a corp may place at tick 0 — first cut: extraction, one food route, one fuel route. Everything else is earned, by depth (BL-586’s chains) or by tech (BL-588’s gates).
2. **Re-check the `any`-band escape.** An `any`-band recipe is never depth-filtered, per the 2026-08-16 first-cut ruling. With a wide ancient roster that exemption becomes load-bearing in the wrong direction — it is how a group stays open when all its ancient members are locked. Either the ancient band gets its own representative selection, or the exemption narrows. State the call; do not let it stand as a default.
3. **The assertion**, in `chain_depth`: at reached depth 0 with no techs earned, the count of placeable ancient buildings is at or below the authored opening set — and every one of the rest is reachable by SOME sequence. The no-stranded-recipe row already present, applied to the opening rather than to the ceiling.

## The failure this guards against

A narrow opening that is narrow because something is unreachable is worse than a wide one. `chain_depth` already states the principle: an unplaceable building is the roster’s orphan. Both halves — few at the start, all of them eventually — must be asserted together, or tuning will satisfy one by breaking the other.

items.title: Every building in the game is made of steel — construction materials key off the type, not the building
items.summary: RULING 2026-08-23 (Ben): materials vary per named building. Measured: resource_build_cost sits on building_economics, which is keyed by building_type, so all eight types cost steel and nothing else — the launchpad alone adds refined fuel. An ancient world whose every structure is smelted steel is the same anachronism the launchpad’s era tag was written to remove, and it leaves timber, stone, clay and the BL-585 goods with one recipe sink apiece and no construction sink at all.
items.design:
## The shape of the change

`resource_build_cost` stays where it is as the DEFAULT for a type. What is added is an override keyed by the named building — the pair that already identifies one everywhere else in the codebase:

  * extraction: `(building_type, target_resource)`
  * processing: `(building_type, recipe)`

Authored in `economy.lua` beside the type’s own entry. Absent means the type default, so nothing that does not opt in changes.

## Where it is read

Eight call sites across five files read `econ.resource_build_cost` directly today: `construction.cpp` (the real gate), `economy_system.cpp` (three — the per-tick material draw during construction), `selection_panel.cpp` (the Build door’s capex figure, and the road path), `construction_panel.cpp`. Every one goes through a single lookup, for the reason BL-436 records about richness: **a preview that disagrees with the tick prices a building the economy will not deliver.** The door’s `capex` and `material_rate` are previews of exactly this number.

## What it buys, beyond flavour

A second sink for the shallow goods. Timber, stone, clay and dressed stone become things a corp needs because it is BUILDING, not only because a recipe consumes them — which is the demand that makes an early quarry worth owning. It also gives the depth ladder a second bite: a deep building can cost a deep good.

## Watch

`corp_ai.cpp` prices candidates through the same estimate, so the scorer picks the change up for free — but a building whose materials a corp cannot reach becomes a candidate it will score and then fail to place. Check the candidate filter; do not assume it.

items.title: A corp’s reached depth gates six places and is displayed in none of them
items.summary: RULING 2026-08-23 (Ben): the readout goes on the corporation dashboard. Measured: corp_reached_depth has six call sites and every one of them GATES — construction, the recipe switch, the AI scorer, and two filters in the Build door. None displays. The Depth page was cut outright in the 2026-08-15 playtest rework, so the growth track this whole minor is named for is only ever felt as a row that is not there.
items.design:
## The question the surface answers (BL-260 discipline)

**“How far down the production graph has my company actually got, and what does the next rung open?”**

It is a corporation-grain fact — `corp_reached_depth` reads `corporation_component::produced_ever` — which is why the building card was the wrong home for it and the dashboard is the right one. The 2026-08-15 rework cut it for the right reason; the idea was not what was wrong.

## Content

Three lines, no more:

1. **Reached depth**, and the good that set it — the deepest thing the corp has ever made. Produced-once-ever, never cleared, so the number only rises.
2. **What the next rung opens** — the buildings whose `recipe_required_depth` is exactly `reached + 1`.
3. **What is missing to get there** — the input those recipes need that the corp has never produced. This is the line that turns a lock into an instruction.

## Constraints

The dashboard is four cards with an in-place expansion and a full-canvas takeover (BL-265). This is a Production-card concern rather than a fifth card — confirm on sight, not by argument. Rule 0b applies: state the current measurements before reshaping, and open the live app before asking Ben to judge it.

A rival’s reached depth is **private** and must not appear. The Method and Profitability pages are already withheld from a rival card for exactly this reason, and under spectator god view the rule is sight, never hands.

## Owed alongside the code

`question_log.json` entry written WITH the surface, not after. A user story on the intent axis — there is nothing on “know how far my production has reached” today. No `ACTIONS.json` entry: this is a readout, not a control.

**A live click before the visual requirement is marked complete**, per the standing rule — a capture proves it renders, not that the card is reachable.

items.title: The breadth invariants — methods win somewhere, the opening is narrow, and the wide roster strands nothing
items.summary: The sprint’s assertions, gathered into the harness that already owns the roster invariants rather than into a new one. chain_depth carries R1 (no orphans), R1b (none inside a band), R2 (no dominant method) and G1-G4 (the gate). This item grows R2 to a second price snapshot, adds the start-gate and materials rows, and re-runs the orphan rows against a roster that has roughly doubled.
items.design:
## Rows

1. **R2 gains a second price vector.** Today it compares one fixed reference snapshot, which cannot see a method that is better “depending on which market it builds to” (Ben, 2026-08-23) — such a method reads as dominated. Two vectors, fuel-cheap and fuel-dear; a genuine interchangeable method must win under at least one. A method that wins under neither is dead content and fails the row.
2. **The start-gate row** (BL-589): at reached depth 0 with no techs earned, placeable ancient buildings are at or below the authored opening set — AND every withheld one is reachable by some sequence. Both halves or neither; a narrow opening bought with an unreachable building is worse than a wide one.
3. **A materials row** (BL-590): every named building’s material basket is obtainable in its own band. A quarry costing a good only the industrial arc makes is unbuildable at 0 CE, and nothing else in the suite would catch it.
4. **R1/R1b re-run** across BL-585’s appends. The rows already exist, but they ARE the sprint’s admission rule and should be named in its requirement rather than assumed to still pass.

## Why not a new harness

`chain_depth` already owns the recipe graph, loads the shipped Lua, and holds the roster invariants. A second harness would need a second reference-price table and would give two answers to one question — which is the stated reason R1 was moved OUT of `recipe_switch_harness` in the first place. Grow the one that owns it.

Naming the new rows in `.claude/skills/verifier-headless/SKILL.md` is part of this item, not a follow-up (CLAUDE.md § Tool creation is skill creation).

items.title: The Build door was shaped for four processing rows and is about to be handed a roster twice the size
items.summary: The UI half of the content sprint. The door groups candidates by family and collapses processing to one row per sub-facility group, choosing the highest-expected-profit era-allowed recipe as each group’s representative. That shape holds at four groups; at eight or more, with a third lock kind to explain and per-building material baskets to price, it needs a pass. A roster the player cannot browse is a data file, not content.
items.design:
## What changes underneath it

  * **More groups.** BL-586 adds at least one (Construction Materials) and probably two. The representative-recipe rule was written for four.
  * **A third lock to explain.** `era_locked`, `depth_locked`, and now `tech_locked` on a recipe (BL-588) are three different answers to “why can I not build this”, and they resolve differently — never, by building, by researching. The door’s current behaviour is to FILTER depth-locked ancient recipes out entirely: defensible for a lock whose rule the player cannot see, and wrong for one they are meant to work toward.
  * **Material baskets vary** (BL-590), so capex is no longer one number per type and the pre-commit material warning has more to say.

## The call to put to Ben, with the app open

Filtered-out versus shown-and-locked. Rule 0b: state the row counts under each before asking. The argument for showing is BL-591’s — an invisible gate reads as a bug. The argument for filtering is that the door already refuses to offer what the gate would refuse, and a door of locks is not a door.

## Owed alongside the code

`question_log.json` for any surface this earns. `ACTIONS.json` transcribed from the seam verb once it exists, never authored ahead of it (BL-270 discipline). The toggle rule applies to anything foldable. **A live click before the visual requirement flips complete.**

items.title: Play the ancient arc from a narrow opening to a deep chain, then cut v0.1.17
items.summary: The sprint’s own done-definition, played rather than asserted. Start a 0 CE campaign, verify the opening is narrow, climb the ladder by building rather than by waiting, choose a production method for a reason, and read the reached depth off the dashboard. Then cut the minor with a done-definition written at the cut, per NR-103.
items.design:
## The playthrough

One session, played end to end, each step written down as it happens:

1. A fresh ancient corp is offered the authored opening set and no more (BL-589).
2. Building a fuel route makes the next rung placeable — and it is legible WHY, from the dashboard readout (BL-591), not from a wiki.
3. A method choice is made for a stated reason, and the reason is about which market the output is going to (BL-587).
4. A tech gate resolves and opens a recipe that is different rather than stronger (BL-588).
5. A building is placed whose material basket is not steel (BL-590).

## What counts as failure

A step that only works because the harness says so. The standing rule is explicit: a scripted capture proves a surface renders, not that a press on it is reachable. Every UI step above is a live click.

## The cut

The v0.1.17 tag, with a done-definition written AT the cut (NR-103). ROADMAP’s v0.1.17 bullet reconciled to what actually shipped — it currently names six items, three of which landed and three of which this sprint replaces. The Sprint 17 retro filled in against its goal. MANUAL.md gains the ancient roster and the earned locks: the player-facing half of a content sprint is the manual entry, not only the door.
